status: Unofficial results with all 57 tabulators reported. The Town Clerk declares the official results.

sections.title: Turnout
sections.headline: One in three electors voted, and ballots rose by nearly half since 2022
points: Two in three eligible electors did not vote. That is why winners can take office with a small share of residents: the new mayor's 21,866 votes equal 12.4% of eligible electors.
Advance voting grew 37%, yet its share of all ballots fell from 26.4% to 24.4%. Election-day voting grew even faster, which points to late deciders and a high-interest race at the top of the ballot.

Ward 7 cast the fewest ballots of any ward: 5,846, or 9.6% of the town total, against an average of 8,663 per ward. Ward 4 cast the most at 12,400. The Town does not publish electors by ward, so exact ward turnout cannot be calculated from its results.
Some voters skip races further down the ballot. 422 ballots (0.7%) had no vote for mayor, against 296 (5.1%) for Ward 7 Town and Regional and 290 (5.0%) for Ward 7 Town Councillor.
In Ward 7, the Town and Regional race drew 61% more votes than in 2022 (3,438 to 5,550), and the Town Councillor race 58% more (3,527 to 5,556).

sections.title: Mayor
sections.headline: Jeff Knoll elected mayor with 36.3%. Rob Burton, mayor since 2006, finishes third

cards.l: vote margin over Sean O'Meara (13.8 points)

points: A clear change vote: 79.6% of voters chose someone other than the incumbent, while turnout rose almost 48%.
Knoll won a plurality, not a majority. 63.7% voted for another candidate, which is normal in a five-way race.
Vote splitting did not decide the winner. The anti-incumbent vote spread across Knoll, O'Meara and Hanna, but Knoll still finished 8,299 votes ahead of second place.
The two sitting councillors in the race finished first and second. Years of ward-level name recognition carried them town-wide.
Julia Hanna fell from 47.1% in the 2022 two-way race to 17.7%. A crowded field changes the math completely.
The Town publishes the mayoral result town-wide only, so there is no ward-by-ward mayor breakdown.

sections.title: Ward 7 Town Councillor
sections.headline: Scott Xie re-elected with a majority of 54.5%

cards.l: vote margin over Zulfi Malik (24.9 points)

points: Xie went from 23.3% in a nine-way race in 2022 to a majority in a three-way race. Four years in office let him consolidate.
Zulfi Malik placed second with 29.6% and Ali Hosny third with 15.9%.
Both Ward 7 races were on the same 5,846 ballots. The gap between the two incumbents (Xie 54.5%, Nanda 40.5%) comes from the candidates, not from turnout.

sections.title: Ward 7 Town & Regional
sections.headline: Nav Nanda re-elected with 40.5%. Bilal Kader second, 376 votes behind

cards.l: votes for the other three candidates (25.9%)

points: Second-closest council race in Oakville tonight by votes, after Ward 5 Town Councillor (202 votes).
The incumbent held the seat but lost ground. His share fell from 57.7% to 40.5%. He added 261 votes (+13%) while total votes in the race rose 61%, so almost all new votes went to challengers.

Of the five races with a sitting councillor on the ballot, this gave the incumbent his lowest share (40.5%) and the challenger his highest (33.7%). The others: Chisholm 73.1%, Longo 80.4%, Lishchyna 65.1%, Xie 54.5%.
The other three candidates took 1,436 votes, almost four times the winning margin. Vick Walia led them with 833 (15.0%).
The arithmetic of the gap: 189 voters switching from Nanda to Kader, or 377 more net votes for Kader, would have changed the result.
